requirements.title: A nonparenthesized primary gets its characteristics from its primary alternative
requirements.definition: The type, type parameters, and shape of a primary are determined by which primary alternative appears. Literal constants, constructors, array constructors, designators, function references, generic function references, type parameter inquiries, and type parameter names take the characteristics specified for those alternatives in their owning subclauses; type parameter inquiries and type parameter names are scalar integers with the kind of the type parameter.

review_rationale: batch104: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 18 base units of 10.1.9.1, 10.1.9.2 and 10.1.9.3 in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verified 18 base / 49 fine units, 24 requirements and 81 facets (all pending), and independently confirmed the accounting claim that the packet newly accounts only 10 base units rather than 18: the eight numbered units R1025, C1007, R1026, C1008, R1027, C1009, R1028 and C1010 were already accounted by the numbered-rule inventory, and the reviewer verified each is neither double-counted nor dropped. The four permission dispositions were each checked and accepted: the 10.1.9.2 p3 disassociated-pointer phrase only allows contexts explicitly permitted elsewhere, and the three 10.1.9.3 p4 processor-dependent result-kind choices are not promoted to requirements. On the known mixed-kind trap the reviewer derived the rules independently before comparing: integer with real or complex uses the real or complex operand kind; different-range integer pairs require the greater RANGE kind and different-precision real or complex pairs the greater PRECISION kind; but equal-range integer, equal-precision real or complex, and different-kind logical results require only that the kind be one of the operand kinds, with the choice processor dependent. No pending plan hard-codes a kind value, predicts which operand kind is selected, or assumes that multiple nondefault kinds exist; plans compare KIND, LEN, RANGE and PRECISION against declarations, operands or dynamically discovered supported kinds. Vacuity was checked: LEN is explicit for character length, disassociated and unallocated arrays are given no SHAPE oracle, and the binary-operation shape plan warns that two conformable arrays cannot discriminate the x1-shape rule. No table is a base unit in this scope; Table 10.2 is cited as a dependency of already-registered 10.1.5.1 and not duplicated. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings; two non-blocking observations recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_104.json. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
